newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen down on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen down on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares on Friday rose for the third straight session but analysts said the strong selling after price-fixing suggested the market, currently at 14,484.8 points, might have problems piercing resistance at 14,500.
They said investors might believe that the expected institutional buying at the start of the year actually began in mid-December and had led to profit-taking.
"It seems that those who thought there might be a 'January effect' bought in December...and now there could be falls," said Pawel Tarnowski of Raiffeisen Capital & Investment.
The main market has risen nine percent since December 10.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.4 percent to 14,484.8 points and turnover rose 24.7 percent to 84.8 million zlotys ($29.5 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 61 to 11 with 11 stocks flat.
Analysts said top gainer construction firm Espebepe, up 9.8 percent in light trade, was continuing to enjoy a speculative rise after having fallen most of the year on a bankruptcy threat.
Analysts were surprised by the scale of drug maker Jelfa's 9.3-percent jump in moderate trade and biggest loser Bank Komunalny's 9.8-percent drop in light trade.
Mass privatisation NFI units eased 0.3 percent to 143 zlotys ($49.8) in 6.4-million-zloty ($2.2 million) trade.
